Some of you may be familiar with the Duke lacrosse case, a scandal where lacrosse players at Duke were falsely accused of rape and subjected to a very unfair process. Many people think none of that is over, and that it was simply the beginning of an avalanche effect in which male students at universities have been increasingly demonized and a climate of paranoia over gender relations has developed. An oft-quoted statistic (questioned by many) is that 1 in 5 women on campus will be a victim of sexual assault, which has been described as a reflection of a 'rape culture' in American society.

It is under this context that Title IX has gained controversy. Under Title IX, universities have an obligation to investigate any complaints of a sexual nature by students, and any university which fails to comply with it risks losing its federal funding. In principle, Title IX is meant to protect students from sexual discrimination, yet, it has been claimed that Title IX has been misused recently, in that it is used to unfairly prosecute male students without due process. For instance, many universities have policies in which the defendant is not allowed to cross-examine the accuser, and in which he is not allowed to have a lawyer representing him. Sometimes they won't even know what they're being accused of or what the evidence is until the day of the hearing.

Needless to say, we have the makings of a saga with ever-more Kafkaesque iterations. The latest I know of are a series of cases in which professors have been accused under Title IX of 'retaliation' or 'harassment' simply for writing opinion pieces in which they disagree with how certain complaints in relation to other cases were handled. This happened to Laura Kipnis, a female feminist professor who found herself under investigation because a student filed a harassment complaint 'on behalf of' another student which wasn't even named on the article, and which she didn't even know.

Of course, many people out there see in this a SJW conspiracy to take over universities and stifle free speech. That is controversial, but something most people agree on is that Title IX is being misused (the Harvard Law faculty have criticised it heavily). So, what do you people think? What caused this (someone has elsewhere has mentioned helicopter parents)? Is this the end of free speech? Will there be a turn away from this, or is the process irreversible?
